newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Buba's Sievert - mark level not fully corrected.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Sievert - mark level not fully corrected.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Olaf Sievert said on Friday the German mark had not yet fully corrected its levels against the currencies of its major trading partners since 1994 and 1995.

"The mark's real exchange rate against our chief trading partners...rose strongly in 1994 and 1995, an incorrect development which has eased significantly this year, but not yet fully," Sievert said in a speech at a banking conference in Salzburg.
A copy of the speech was available in advance in Frankfurt. Real exchange rates account for differences in inflation rates.

Development in the 1990s on forex markets had probably contributed to the unusually stubborn phase of economic stagnation in Germany, Sievert added, from which the country had only started to escape in the second quarter of 1996.
Sievert also hit out against "timid" supporters of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) who refused to acknowledge that the arrival of the single currency could help solve employment problems.
"Improving the way the labour market functions, making it easier to correct market imbalances, that seems to me the most important expectation that one can pin on monetary union," Sievert said.
"There will be no more currency fluctuations to make jobs, or investment in jobs, unpredictably uncompetitive and thus, unprofitable," he said.
